dedupe_keys.name: yearly extent of surface coal mining in central appalachia 1985 2015 skytruth and duke university landsat and google earth engine

description: Annual maps of active surface coal mining in the Central Appalachian region of the United States from 1985 to 2015, made from Landsat imagery in Google Earth Engine for the 2018 PLOS One paper "Mapping the yearly extent of surface coal mining in Central Appalachia using Landsat and Google Earth Engine". The figshare items, published in May 2018 by Andrew A. Pericak and nine co-authors, give one GeoTIFF per year of active mining (about 7 MB each), plus cumulative mining area, first and most recent mining year, mine permit boundaries, a processing mask and the study area, in GeoTIFF, shapefile, GeoJSON and KML, together with the Earth Engine JavaScript used to build them. The files are free for download under Apache 2.0. A companion figshare dataset published in 2022 (CC BY 4.0) gives annual vegetation index trajectories for reclaimed sites, for the Restoration Ecology paper "Mines to Forests?". Caveats: yearly files show where mining occurred in a year but not when it began or ended, and the method detects surface mining only. For simulation it gives a 31-year land disturbance series for studying cumulative mining footprints, reclamation and exposure of nearby streams and communities. A related catalogue record is the Maus global mining polygons dataset.
